candidates.title: Boat cruise to Bonaventure Island and Percé Rock
candidates.summary: Boat trip around Percé Rock to Bonaventure Island, where you can walk to the northern gannet colony. It covers one of the stops the party already wants and suits an 11- and 7-year-old at moderate effort. Access needs were not answered, so trail and boat accessibility is unaccounted for.

candidates.title: Cap-Gaspé walk at Forillon
candidates.summary: A moderate coastal walk to the Cap-Gaspé lighthouse at the end of the peninsula, with chances to see seals and whales. It covers the requested Forillon stop. Access needs were not answered, and the trail may not suit every mobility level.

candidates.title: Grande-Grave heritage site, Forillon
candidates.summary: Restored fishing-village buildings and an easy shoreline stroll. It is short and kid-friendly, which makes it a good break from the car. Accessibility is unknown.

candidates.title: Percé Géoparc glass platform
candidates.summary: A glass lookout high above Percé with views of the rock, plus short trails. It is a compact outing for the kids. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Fossils at Miguasha National Park
candidates.summary: A UNESCO fossil site on the south shore loop with a natural history museum and a beach walk. It gives the trip something new on the Baie-des-Chaleurs side, away from the north shore they have already done. Accessibility is unknown.

candidates.title: Reford Gardens (Jardins de Métis)
candidates.summary: Large historic gardens that make a good leg-stretching stop to break up the drive, with space for kids to roam. Access needs were not answered.

candidates.title: Bioparc de la Gaspésie
candidates.summary: A small zoo of Gaspé wildlife that is easy for a 7-year-old and sits on the south shore return route. Accessibility is unknown.

candidates.title: Observatoire de la Capitale
candidates.summary: A 31st-floor lookout over Québec City that works as a short break on the first or last driving leg. Listed hours are 10:00 to 17:40. Accessibility was not checked.

candidatesAccepted.title: Highway 20 east along the south shore with a Kamouraska stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: First driving leg, broken at the riverside village of Kamouraska so the seven-year-old gets out of the car well before three hours. It stays on the south shore, which keeps it new to a family that has already done the north shore. Access needs were not answered, so stop accessibility is not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Lower St. Lawrence coast drive with a Reford Gardens stop
candidatesAccepted.summary: Follows the coast on Route 132, with Jardins de Métis as a natural leg-stretch stop. The garden entry fee is not included in the cost band.

candidatesAccepted.title: Northern Gaspé coastal drive toward Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: A dramatic cliff-and-cove stretch of Route 132 with many pull-offs, which suits a family that would rather stop often. It ends at Forillon, one of the stops they already want. Park entry fees are not included.

candidatesAccepted.title: Short coastal transfer to the Percé Rock area
candidatesAccepted.summary: A short drive to Percé Rock, another of their chosen stops, leaving room for the boat out to Bonaventure Island. The boat fare is not included.

candidatesAccepted.title: Baie-des-Chaleurs south coast drive, completing the loop
candidatesAccepted.summary: Returns along the gentler south coast so the trip is a true loop with nothing repeated. There are frequent beaches and towns to stop at.

candidatesAccepted.title: Matapédia Valley crossing back to the river
candidatesAccepted.summary: A forested river-valley drive inland, rejoining the St. Lawrence before the run home. The final stretch back to Montréal still needs to be split into further parts, which this leg does not cover.

candidatesAccepted.title: Serviced campsite with showers, Forillon National Park
candidatesAccepted.summary: Parks Canada campgrounds in Forillon (e.g., Petit-Gaspé) have showers and suit a simple-night family of four near a must-see stop. Access needs were not answered, so accessibility of sites is unaccounted for; July sites typically sell out when reservations open.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel near Percé Rock
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple family motel room in Percé puts the party a short walk from the rock and Bonaventure boat departures. Access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Ready-to-camp tent or cabin, Parc national de la Gaspésie
candidatesAccepted.summary: SEPAQ ready-to-camp units or rustic cabins near Mont-Albert break up the inland/south leg with a simple, shower-served night. Accessibility not accounted for since access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Campground with showers, Parc national de Miguasha area
candidatesAccepted.summary: A serviced campground or cabin on the Baie-des-Chaleurs side gives the south-shore return leg something new. Access needs not answered and not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Family motel stopover in the Lower St. Lawrence
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple motel splits the long drive from Montréal into half-day legs for the seven-year-old. Access needs not answered and not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Motel or inn in the Matapédia Valley
candidatesAccepted.summary: A simple roadside motel in Amqui gives a short-hop rest on the inland return, avoiding the north shore. Access needs not answered and not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Fish and chips or lobster roll at a Percé seafood counter
candidatesAccepted.summary: A casual seafood counter in Percé puts local catch in front of the rock you came to see, and kids can eat simple fried fish. Dietary restrictions and access needs were not answered, so check menus and entry yourself.

candidatesAccepted.title: Smoked fish tasting at Fumoir d'Antan
candidatesAccepted.summary: A family-run traditional herring and salmon smokehouse near Gaspé, a short, kid-sized stop that breaks up driving around Forillon. Hours, season and access not verified; dietary needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Bakery stop in Kamouraska
candidatesAccepted.summary: Kamouraska on the south shore route out has bakeries worth a leg-stretch for the seven-year-old, and this shore is new to the family. No specific premises verified; dietary needs not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Sea-side picnic from a Matane shrimp shop
candidatesAccepted.summary: Matane is known for its northern shrimp; buying from a fish shop and picnicking by the water is cheap, flexible and good for kids who need a break from the car. Shop and season not verified; dietary needs not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Gaspésie microbrewery pub meal in Carleton-sur-Mer
candidatesAccepted.summary: A family-friendly brewpub dinner on the Baie des Chaleurs side of the loop, with local food and non-alcoholic options for the kids. Specific premises not verified; dietary and access needs not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Forillon National Park day entry and family hiking
candidatesAccepted.summary: A requested stop with short coastal trails suited to a 7- and 11-year-old. The band assumes the Parks Canada family/group daily pass, and paid activities are excluded. Access needs were not answered, so trail suitability for every traveller is unaccounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Boat cruise to Île Bonaventure from Percé
candidatesAccepted.summary: A view of Percé Rock up close plus the gannet colony, a highlight for kids. The band assumes adult and child fares together with park entry to the island, and it is per person. Accessibility of the boarding is unknown because access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Serviced campsite with showers at Forillon
candidatesAccepted.summary: Keeps lodging cheap while meeting the showers requirement and a 'simple' comfort level. The band assumes an unserviced or partly serviced site per night, and July demand means reserving early. It covers the tent site only; gear and food are excluded.

candidatesAccepted.title: Fuel for the loop from Montréal
candidatesAccepted.summary: The biggest unavoidable road-trip cost. The band assumes roughly 2,000–2,400 km in a mid-size car at July 2027 Québec pump prices, which are a guess. It covers the whole route for the party, while tolls and ferries are not included.
